items.title: Section: The Four Perceptions Close Cultivation Through Perception

items.zh: 或修涅槃道時，於斷界、離欲界、滅界觀見最勝寂靜功德，修習斷想、離欲想、滅想。或修奢摩他時，修習止品上下想。或修毘鉢舍那時，修習觀品前後想。上下想者，謂觀察此身如其所住、如其所願。上從頂上，下至足下，種種雜類不淨充滿。謂此身中所有種種髮、毛、爪、齒，如前廣說。前後想者，謂如有一，於所觀相殷勤懇到，善取、善思、善了、善達。謂住觀於坐，坐觀於臥，或在後行觀察前行。此則顯示以毘鉢舍那行，觀察三世緣生諸行。謂若說言：住觀於坐。此則顯示以現在作意，觀察未來所知諸行。所以者何？現在作意位，已現生故，說名為住；未來所知位，未現生故，臨欲起故，說名為坐。若復說言：坐觀於臥。此則顯示以現在作意，觀察過去所知諸行。所以者何？現在作意位，臨欲滅故，說名為坐；過去所知位，已謝滅故，說名為臥。若復說言：或在後行觀察前行。此則顯示以現在作意，觀無間滅現行作意。所以者何？若已生起無間謝滅所取作意，說名前行；若此無間新新生起能取作意，取前無間已謝滅者，說名後行。當知此中，為修止觀，修彼二品勝光明想，是名想修。
items.en: Or, when cultivating the path to nirvana, one cultivates the perception of cessation, the perception of dispassion, and the perception of extinction, seeing the most excellent, peaceful virtue in the sphere of cessation, the sphere of dispassion, and the sphere of extinction. Or, when cultivating calm-abiding, one cultivates the top-to-bottom perception belonging to the calming category. Or, when cultivating insight, one cultivates the before-and-after perception belonging to the observing category. … Abiding observes sitting; sitting observes lying down; or what comes later observes what came before. This shows the practice of insight observing the conditioned formations of the three times. … Know that, for the sake of cultivating calm-abiding and insight, cultivating these two categories' excellent luminous perception is called cultivation through perception.

items.title: Section: Cultivation Through the Factors of Enlightenment Opens — Foundations and Efforts

items.zh: 云何菩提分修？謂於三十七菩提分法親近積集，若修、若習、若多修習，是名菩提分修。何等名為三十七種菩提分法？謂四念住、四正斷、四神足、五根、五力、七覺支、八聖道。四念住者，一、身念住，二、受念住，三、心念住，四、法念住。四正斷者，一、於已生惡不善法為令斷故，生欲、策勵、發勤精進，策心、持心、正斷。二、於未生惡不善法為不生故，生欲、策勵、發勤精進，策心、持心、正斷。三、於未生善法為令生故，生欲、策勵、發勤精進，策心、持心、正斷。四、於已生善法為欲令住、令不忘失、令修圓滿、令倍修習、令其增長、令其廣大，生欲、策勵、發勤精進，策心、持心、正斷。
items.en: What is cultivation through the factors of enlightenment? It is closely engaging, gathering, practising, repeating, and thoroughly cultivating the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment. What are these thirty-seven factors? The four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path. The four foundations of mindfulness are: mindfulness of the body, of feeling, of mind, and of phenomena. The four right efforts are: generating aspiration, exerting oneself, and diligently applying energy — spurring, sustaining, and rightly directing the mind — in order to end unwholesome states already arisen; to prevent unwholesome states not yet arisen from arising; to give rise to wholesome states not yet arisen; and to make wholesome states already arisen abide, not be forgotten, be brought to completion, be doubled, increased, and made vast.

items.title: Bases of Power Through the Eightfold Path

items.zh: 四神足者，一、欲三摩地斷行成就神足，二、勤三摩地斷行成就神足，三、心三摩地斷行成就神足，四、觀三摩地斷行成就神足。五根者，一、信根，二、精進根，三、念根，四、定根，五、慧根。五力者，一、信力，二、精進力，三、念力，四、定力，五、慧力。七覺支者，一、念等覺支，二、擇法等覺支，三、精進等覺支，四、喜等覺支，五、安等覺支，六、定等覺支，七、捨等覺支。八支聖道者，一、正見，二、正思惟，三、正語，四、正業，五、正命，六、正精進，七、正念，八、正定。
items.en: The four bases of power are: the basis of power through concentration accompanied by aspiration and the abandoning of unwholesome activity; through concentration accompanied by diligence; through concentration accompanied by mind; and through concentration accompanied by investigation. The five faculties are: the faculty of faith, of diligence, of mindfulness, of concentration, and of wisdom. The five powers are: the power of faith, of diligence, of mindfulness, of concentration, and of wisdom. The seven factors of enlightenment are: the factor of mindfulness, of investigation of phenomena, of diligence, of joy, of pliancy, of concentration, and of equanimity. The eightfold noble path is: right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right concentration.

items.title: Body Mindfulness in Detail: Thirty-Five Kinds of Bodily Aspect

items.zh: 今於此中，云何為身？云何於身住循身觀？云何為念？云何念住？略說身相有三十五。謂內身、外身、根所攝身、非根所攝身、有情數身、非有情數身、麁重俱行身、輕安俱行身、能造身、所造身、名身、色身、那落迦身、傍生身、祖父國身、人身、天身、有識身、無識身、中身、表身、變異身、不變異身、女身、男身、半擇迦身、親友身、非親友身、中庸身、劣身、中身、妙身、幼身、少身、老身。如是名為身相差別。
items.en: Here, what is the body? What is dwelling in observation of the body? What is mindfulness? What is the establishment of mindfulness? Briefly, the aspects of the body are thirty-five: internal and external body; body included in the faculties and not so included; body belonging to sentient beings and not so belonging; body bound up with grossness and with pliancy; the causal-element body and the derived body; the name-body and the form-body … the human body and the divine body; the conscious body and the unconscious body; the inner body and the outwardly-presented body; the changed body and the unchanged body; the female, male, and neuter body; the body of a friend, of a non-friend, and of a neutral party; the inferior, middling, and excellent body; the young, mature, and aged body. These are called the differentiations of bodily aspect.

blocks.text: Cultivation through perception and through the thirty-seven factors of awakening. Then the treatise begins a detailed account of the **four foundations of mindfulness**, starting with the body.

"When cultivating the path to nirvāṇa, one cultivates the perceptions of abandonment, dispassion, and cessation, seeing the most excellent, peaceful vision." Master Cháng Bǎi links them to the fruits. And a striking image of examination: "abiding observes sitting; sitting observes lying down; what comes later observes what came before". Venerable Miào Jìng: one stage of practice checks the one before.

"Closely engaging, gathering, practising, repeating, thoroughly cultivating" the thirty-seven: four foundations of mindfulness, four right efforts, four bases of power, five faculties, five powers, seven factors of awakening, the eightfold path.

subs.head: Bases of power and the path

blocks.text: The four bases of power: concentration through aspiration, diligence, mind, and investigation, "accompanied by the abandoning of unwholesome activity". And the eightfold path: right view through right concentration.

"What is the body? What is dwelling in observation of the body? What is mindfulness? What is the establishment of mindfulness?" The body has thirty-five aspects: internal and external, the faculties and their supports, the name-body and form-body, the bodies of beings in each realm, and so on. Venerable Miào Jìng: the name-body is feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness; the form-body is the physical body.

quiz.q: What are the two kinds of cultivation, and what does Master Cháng Bǎi say the perception of fault is?
options: through perception and through the factors of enlightenment; the perception of fault is the six-aspect contemplation — rejecting the lower as painful, coarse, obstructive, seeking the higher as calm, sublime, free
quiz.why: "Cultivation through perception, and cultivation through the factors of enlightenment." Master Cháng Bǎi: rejecting the lower as painful, coarse, and obstructing, seeking the higher as calm, sublime, and freeing — the lower and higher levels compared with each other.

quiz.q: On the path to nirvāṇa one cultivates the perceptions of cessation, dispassion, and extinction. How do the masters map them?
options: Cháng Bǎi: cessation for the first fruit, dispassion up to the fourth, extinction as the arhat's entry into nirvāṇa without remainder; Miào Jìng: the cessation sphere is non-self insight at the path of seeing, extinction is nirvāṇa without remainder
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the perception of cessation realises the first fruit; dispassion, the second, third, and fourth; extinction is the arhat entering nirvāṇa without remainder. Venerable Miào Jìng: the sphere of cessation is really the contemplation of non-self — the path of seeing; the sphere of extinction is nirvāṇa without remainder.

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain "what comes later observes what came before" in insight's before-and-after perception?
options: the former has ceased, the latter has just arisen; the present observes, the previous moment is observed
quiz.why: "Abiding observes sitting; sitting observes lying down; or what comes later observes what came before." Venerable Miào Jìng: the former has already ceased, the latter is presently arising; what presently arises observes, and the previous moment is what is observed.

quiz.q: Into which seven groups are the thirty-seven factors divided, and how does Venerable Miào Jìng explain 分?
options: the four foundations, efforts, bases of power, five faculties, powers, seven factors, eightfold path; awakening is the fruit, 分 the cause
quiz.why: "The four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path." Venerable Miào Jìng: awakening is the fruit, 分 the cause; from cause comes fruit — "factors of awakening" means causes of awakening.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi map the eightfold path to the three trainings?
options: view and intention are wisdom; speech, action, livelihood discipline; mindfulness and concentration concentration; effort spans all three
quiz.why: "Right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right concentration." Master Cháng Bǎi: right view and intention are wisdom; speech, action, and livelihood are discipline; mindfulness and concentration belong to concentration; right effort spans all three.

quiz.q: How many bodily aspects does the treatise list, and how does Master Cháng Bǎi group them?
options: thirty-five, in fourteen groups: internal and external, faculty and non-faculty, sentient and non-sentient, and so on
quiz.why: "Briefly, the aspects of the body are thirty-five." Master Cháng Bǎi: the bodily aspects are thirty-five, in fourteen groups — internal and external, included in the faculties or not, sentient or not, and so on.

quiz.q: The note reads 名身 as the mere name "body." What do the masters say?
options: both agree: the name-body is feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — mind; body mindfulness should take only the form-body as object
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: the name-body is feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness; the form-body is the physical body. Master Cháng Bǎi: it refers to the mental factors of feeling and the rest, which should not count in body mindfulness, which takes only form as its object.
